_note: This is the game's DEFAULT style — used for room backgrounds, room props and in-room character sprites. Cutscene-only portrait art bypasses this file with hand-written prompts. HISTORY, in one day: (1) close-up cinematic-portrait camera used for rooms by mistake — looked like a photo backdrop with cutouts standing in front; (2) fixed the camera angle but kept painterly/vignette rendering — still murky, user said 'think Stardew Valley'; (3) went fully flat cel-shaded Stardew — user said that 'doesn't fit the bill' and pointed back at the inspiration images and the already-generated portraits as the real target: richly saturated, moody, warm-vs-cool lit, textured. (4) THE CURRENT ONE, and the reason this file changed shape: a room used to be generated as ONE picture with its furniture painted into it, and everything downstream fought that. The walkable floor had to be reverse-engineered out of the picture by hand (five techniques tried and abandoned — see build_walkmask.py), a painted tree was something you could only be fenced away from, never walk behind, and re-placing one object meant regenerating the whole room. Rooms are now generated in TWO LAYERS.
camera:
Top-down RPG interior room view: a clean, gently-angled overhead perspective, orthogonal walls, a clearly readable floor plane. NEVER an eye-level photograph, NEVER a close-up character-portrait crop.

ROOMS ARE GENERATED IN TWO LAYERS, and a prompt must say which layer it is asking for.

LAYER 1 — THE GROUND PLATE (the room background). The floor, the walls behind it, and things that are genuinely PART of the architecture: wall panelling, shelving built into a wall, a painted rug, a doorway. NOTHING that stands up off the floor out in the room — no free-standing furniture, no trees, no statues, no crates, no tables. The open floor must be wide, unobstructed, and fill most of the lower frame, because that whole area is what the player walks on. This is what makes the walkable-floor mask a wall line and a rectangle instead of a reverse-engineering job.

LAYER 2 — THE PROPS (a separate sheet). Everything that stands up off that floor, drawn SIDE BY SIDE IN ONE IMAGE on flat pure white, each prop upright and whole from base to top, each sitting on the same invisible ground line, no shadow. The game places them, sorts them against the player by foot position and blocks a small ellipse at each one's base — so the player walks BEHIND a tree and stops at its trunk. Cut with .github/art/build_props.py.

IF the ground plate has a door/archway leading elsewhere: it MUST be on the back-right wall, in roughly the rightmost 15-20% of the frame width, with its threshold at floor level (not floating high on the wall) — the walkable exit trigger is placed against it, so a door drawn anywhere else is a door players can see and cannot use. The walkable floor must begin no higher than roughly 45-48% down the frame.
style: Detailed 16-bit pixel art matching this game's own established look (see reference/the-game/inspo-*.png and the character portraits already generated, e.g. michael.png, kat.png) — NOT Stardew Valley's flat cel-shading. Rich, saturated color with real depth: warm light sources (lanterns, windows, candles) casting an actual warm glow against cooler ambient walls/shadow, visible texture on surfaces (brick coursing, wood grain, fabric folds), confident dark outlines. Still requires clean, sharply readable orthogonal architecture — walls meet the floor at a clear line, furniture silhouettes are unambiguous — richness of color/lighting must never come at the cost of the room reading as a coherent walkable space. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: same rich rendering technique and palette as the portrait busts, at a small full-body top-down scale, head-to-feet, clean readable silhouette from the overhead angle.
palette: Saturated, warm-vs-cool contrast — warm amber/gold light pooling against cooler blue, indigo, or wood-brown ambient tone, matching the inspiration images (e.g. inspo-08's warm doorway/window glow against cool blue brick walls). Not evenly lit throughout — real light sources create real pools of brighter warm light against a moodier surrounding tone, as long as the overall room still reads clearly (no area so dark the architecture becomes ambiguous).
background: For a ROOM GROUND PLATE: a complete, atmospherically-lit top-down floor and its surrounding architecture, empty of any characters or people AND empty of free-standing furniture, with an unmistakable open floor filling most of the lower frame. For a PROP SHEET: every prop isolated on FLAT PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF), uniform, hard-edged, with a wide white band between props and a generous white margin — never transparency, which comes back as a beige wash. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: isolated on a transparent background, no scene/ground/shadow drawn in.
constraints: No text, no logos, no watermark, no UI elements, no borders/frames baked into the image. A room ground plate must have clean orthogonal architecture (walls meet the floor at a clear, readable line) — reject anything where the walls look melted, warped or spatially incoherent, but rich atmospheric lighting/colour is expected and desired, not a flaw. STRICTLY no people/characters/figures anywhere in a room, and for a GROUND PLATE strictly nothing standing up off the floor either — both are confirmed failure modes, a stray figure standing in the scene and a room that came back full of painted furniture that then could not be walked behind. A character sprite must be full body head-to-feet, standing, facing the viewer — never a close-up bust crop, and isolated ONLY on plain transparent background with no scene, room, walls, furniture or floor drawn in. Any character wearing glasses must have clearly visible human eyes — pupils and eye whites — showing behind the lenses, never blank/hidden skin tone.
